content.shloka:
Purushottamo maaso yah sarva-paapa-pranaashanah |
Yasmin sampuujito vishnuh sarvaan kaamaan prayachhati ||
content.meaning: The Purushottam month (Adhik Maas) destroys all sins. In this month, when Lord Vishnu is worshipped properly, He grants all desires.
content.transliteration:
Puruṣottamo māso yaḥ sarva-pāpa-praṇāśanaḥ |
Yasmin sampūjito Viṣṇuḥ sarvān kāmān prayacchati ||

content.shloka: Adhik Maas, also known as Purushottam Maas or Mal Maas, is the extra month that occurs approximately every 32.5 months in the Hindu lunar calendar. It is inserted to align the lunar calendar (354 days) with the solar calendar (365 days).
content.meaning: The story goes that this extra month was initially considered inauspicious (Mal Maas = impure month) and no deity wanted to preside over it. Lord Vishnu (Purushottam) graciously accepted it and declared that worship performed in this month yields infinite merit.
content.transliteration: Adhik Maas, also known as Purushottam Maas or Mal Maas, is the extra month that occurs approximately every 32.5 months in the Hindu lunar calendar. It is inserted to align the lunar calendar (354 days) with the solar calendar (365 days).

content.shloka:
Adhik maase tu yat punyam tat punyam naanyamaasake |
Tasmaad adhik maase vishnum archayet bhaktimaan narah ||
content.meaning: The merit earned in Adhik Maas cannot be earned in any other month. Therefore, a devoted person should worship Lord Vishnu in this extra month.
content.transliteration:
Adhik māse tu yat puṇyaṁ tat puṇyaṁ nānyamāsake |
Tasmād adhik māse Viṣṇuṁ arcayet bhaktimān naraḥ ||

content.shloka: No new auspicious events (marriages, house warming, thread ceremony, etc.) are initiated during Adhik Maas. However, it is the most sacred time for spiritual practices — japa, daan, vrat, puja, katha-shravan, and Bhagavat Saptah.
content.meaning: While worldly ceremonies are avoided, Adhik Maas is considered a golden opportunity for spiritual elevation. Every act of devotion performed during this month is multiplied manifold by Lord Purushottam's grace.
content.transliteration: No new auspicious events (marriages, house warming, thread ceremony, etc.) are initiated during Adhik Maas. However, it is the most sacred time for spiritual practices — japa, daan, vrat, puja, katha-shravan, and Bhagavat Saptah.

content.shloka:
Ekaadasham tu yad daanam adhikamaase pradiyate |
Koti-gunam phalam tasya bhagavaan purushottamah ||
content.meaning: The charity (daan) given during Adhik Maas yields results multiplied a crore-fold by the grace of Lord Purushottam.
content.transliteration:
Ekādaśaṁ tu yad dānam adhikamāse pradīyate |
Koṭi-guṇaṁ phalaṁ tasya Bhagavān Puruṣottamaḥ ||

content.shloka: Once upon a time, the twelve months were assigned to twelve deities. But the thirteenth month (Adhik Maas) had no presiding deity. Saddened and humiliated, the extra month approached Lord Vishnu at Vaikuntha.
content.meaning: The month said: 'O Lord, I am called Mal Maas (impure month). No one performs any auspicious activity during my time. I am despised by all. Please be my protector.' Lord Vishnu, moved by compassion, replied...
content.transliteration: Once upon a time, the twelve months were assigned to twelve deities. But the thirteenth month (Adhik Maas) had no presiding deity. Saddened and humiliated, the extra month approached Lord Vishnu at Vaikuntha.

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavaan uvacha: Maa shuchah adhikamaasa, tvam mama priyatamah sadaa |
Mama naamnaa tu vikhyaato bhavishyasi jagattraye ||
content.meaning: Lord Vishnu said: 'Do not grieve, O Adhik Maas. You are forever dear to Me. You shall be known throughout the three worlds by My name — Purushottam Maas.'
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān uvāca: Mā śucaḥ adhikamāsa, tvaṁ mama priyatamaḥ sadā |
Mama nāmnā tu vikhyāto bhaviṣyasi jagat-traye ||

content.shloka: 'Whoever observes a vrat (fast), performs puja, gives charity, or listens to sacred stories during your time shall attain Vaikuntha. The merit earned in your month shall exceed that of all other months combined.'
content.meaning: Lord Vishnu further blessed Adhik Maas: 'Those who read Shrimad Bhagavat during your month shall be freed from the cycle of birth and death. Those who bathe in holy rivers and worship Me with tulsi shall attain My eternal abode.'
content.transliteration: 'Whoever observes a vrat (fast), performs puja, gives charity, or listens to sacred stories during your time shall attain Vaikuntha. The merit earned in your month shall exceed that of all other months combined.'

content.shloka: There was a king named Dridhadhanva who was just but childless. Sage Narada advised him to observe a strict vrat during Adhik Maas with full devotion to Lord Purushottam.
content.meaning: The king fasted, performed daily puja with tulsi, read the Bhagavat Purana, and gave generous charity to Brahmins. Pleased with his devotion, Lord Vishnu appeared and granted him a virtuous son and the promise of Vaikuntha after death.
content.transliteration: There was a king named Dridhadhanva who was just but childless. Sage Narada advised him to observe a strict vrat during Adhik Maas with full devotion to Lord Purushottam.

content.shloka: Iti adhik-maas-vrat-kathaayaam purushottama-maasa-mahaatmyam sampoornam ||
content.meaning: Thus ends the Adhik Maas Vrat Katha describing the glory of Purushottam Maas. One who reads or hears this katha with devotion is blessed by Lord Vishnu.
content.transliteration: Iti adhik-māsa-vrata-kathāyāṁ puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmyaṁ sampūrṇam ||

content.shloka:
Om Namo Bhagavate Vaasudevaaya |
Om Namo Naaraayanaaya |
Om Purushottamaaya Namah ||
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Vasudeva. Salutations to Lord Narayana. Salutations to Lord Purushottam. These three mantras form the foundation of Adhik Maas puja.
content.transliteration:
Om Namo Bhagavate Vāsudevāya |
Om Namo Nārāyaṇāya |
Om Puruṣottamāya Namaḥ ||

content.shloka:
Daily Puja Vidhi for Adhik Maas:
1) Wake before sunrise and take a bath.
2) Set up the puja altar with Lord Vishnu's image or Shaligram Shila.
3) Offer tulsi, flowers, sandalwood paste, and naivedya.
4) Light a ghee diya (lamp) — this should burn throughout the month.
5) Chant Vishnu Sahasranaam or Purushottam Stotra.
content.meaning: The puja should be performed at the same time every day for the entire month. Consistency and devotion are more important than elaborate rituals. Even a simple offering of tulsi and water to Lord Vishnu carries immense merit.
content.transliteration:
Daily Puja Vidhi for Adhik Maas:
1) Wake before sunrise and take a bath.
2) Set up the puja altar with Lord Vishnu's image or Shaligram Shila.
3) Offer tulsi, flowers, sandalwood paste, and naivedya.
4) Light a ghee diya (lamp) — this should burn throughout the month.
5) Chant Vishnu Sahasranaam or Purushottam Stotra.

content.shloka:
Om Shri Vishnave Namah | Om Govindaaya Namah |
Om Madhavaaya Namah | Om Trivikramaaya Namah |
content.meaning: These are the Dwadash Naam (12 names) of Lord Vishnu, each associated with a month. During Adhik Maas, chanting all 12 names carries special significance.
content.transliteration:
Om Śrī Viṣṇave Namaḥ | Om Govindāya Namaḥ |
Om Mādhavāya Namaḥ | Om Trivikramāya Namaḥ |

content.shloka:
Special Activities for Adhik Maas:
- Read Shrimad Bhagavat Purana (complete in 30 days)
- Perform Vishnu Sahasranaam daily
- Observe Ekadashi vrat strictly
- Give charity (daan) of food, clothes, and money
- Feed Brahmins and the poor
- Visit Vishnu temples daily
- Offer 108 tulsi leaves to Shaligram daily
content.meaning: Lord Krishna says in the Bhagavad Gita: 'Among months, I am Margashirsha.' But in Purushottam Maas, He Himself is the presiding deity — making it the most exalted month for devotion.
content.transliteration:
Special Activities for Adhik Maas:
- Read Shrimad Bhagavat Purana (complete in 30 days)
- Perform Vishnu Sahasranaam daily
- Observe Ekadashi vrat strictly
- Give charity (daan) of food, clothes, and money
- Feed Brahmins and the poor
- Visit Vishnu temples daily
- Offer 108 tulsi leaves to Shaligram daily

content.shloka:
Kaayena Vaachaa Manasendriyair Vaa Buddhyaatmanaa Vaa Prakriteh Svabhaavaat |
Karomi Yad Yat Sakalam Parasmai Naaraayanaayeti Samarpayaami ||
content.meaning: Whatever I do with my body, speech, mind, senses, intellect, or soul — whether by nature or by intention — I dedicate everything to Lord Narayana. This closing prayer is chanted after every Adhik Maas puja.
content.transliteration:
Kāyena Vācā Manasendriyair Vā Buddhyātmanā Vā Prakṛteḥ Svabhāvāt |
Karomi Yad Yat Sakalaṁ Parasmai Nārāyaṇāyeti Samarpayāmi ||

content.shloka:
Daanena tapasaa chaiva shauchenaaatithya-poojanaih |
Adhik-maasa-vratam samyak kurvann aapnoti tat phalam ||
content.meaning: Through charity, austerity, purity, and hospitality to guests, one who properly observes the Adhik Maas vrat attains the full fruits of devotion.
content.transliteration:
Dānena tapasā caiva śaucenātithya-pūjanaiḥ |
Adhik-māsa-vrataṁ samyak kurvann āpnoti tat phalam ||

content.shloka:
Recommended Daan (Charity) during Adhik Maas:
1. Anna Daan — Food to the hungry (most meritorious)
2. Vastra Daan — Clothes to the needy
3. Go Daan — Cow donation (or cow shelter support)
4. Jal Daan — Providing drinking water
5. Deepa Daan — Oil lamps at temples
6. Shayyaa Daan — Bedding to the poor
7. Ghat Daan — Copper vessel filled with water, covered with cloth and topped with a coconut
content.meaning: Daan in Adhik Maas is considered infinitely more meritorious than in any other month. The donor should give with humility and without expectation of return. The Ghat Daan is the most distinctive charity of Adhik Maas.
content.transliteration:
Recommended Daan (Charity) during Adhik Maas:
1. Anna Daan — Food to the hungry (most meritorious)
2. Vastra Daan — Clothes to the needy
3. Go Daan — Cow donation (or cow shelter support)
4. Jal Daan — Providing drinking water
5. Deepa Daan — Oil lamps at temples
6. Shayyaa Daan — Bedding to the poor
7. Ghat Daan — Copper vessel filled with water, covered with cloth and topped with a coconut

content.shloka:
Ghat Daan Procedure:
Take a clean copper or brass pot. Fill it with water. Place a betel leaf and a coin inside. Cover with new cloth. Place a coconut on top. Decorate with turmeric and kumkum. Donate to a Brahmin or a temple on the Purnima of Adhik Maas.
content.meaning: The Ghat (pot) symbolizes the universe. Water represents the ocean of existence. The coconut represents the individual soul (jivatma). By donating it, one symbolically offers oneself to the Lord and is freed from the bondage of karma.
content.transliteration:
Ghat Daan Procedure:
Take a clean copper or brass pot. Fill it with water. Place a betel leaf and a coin inside. Cover with new cloth. Place a coconut on top. Decorate with turmeric and kumkum. Donate to a Brahmin or a temple on the Purnima of Adhik Maas.

content.shloka:
Daane tapasi yajna cha paatakam naiva vidyate |
Adhik maase viseshena daanam nityam prakalpayet ||
content.meaning: In charity, austerity, and yajna there is no sin. During Adhik Maas especially, one should practice daily charity.
content.transliteration:
Dāne tapasi yajñe ca pātakaṁ naiva vidyate |
Adhik māse viśeṣeṇa dānaṁ nityaṁ prakalpayet ||

content.shloka:
Annadaanam param daanam vidyaadaanam tatah param |
Annena kshanikaah triptih yaavajjeevam cha vidyayaa ||
content.meaning: The donation of food is a great charity, and the donation of knowledge is even greater. Food satisfies only momentarily, but knowledge provides fulfillment for a lifetime.
content.transliteration:
Annadānaṁ paraṁ dānaṁ vidyādānaṁ tataḥ param |
Annena kṣaṇikāḥ tṛptiḥ yāvajjīvaṁ ca vidyayā ||

content.shloka: Om Namo Bhagavate Vaasudevaaya ||
content.meaning: The twelve-syllable Dwadasakshari Mantra — the most sacred Vishnu mantra. Chanting this 108 times daily during Adhik Maas grants liberation.
content.transliteration: Om Namo Bhagavate Vāsudevāya ||

content.shloka: Om Namo Naaraayanaaya ||
content.meaning: The eight-syllable Ashtakshari Mantra of Lord Narayana. This mantra is considered the essence of all Vedic knowledge and is especially powerful during Purushottam Maas.
content.transliteration: Om Namo Nārāyaṇāya ||

content.shloka:
Om Purushottamaaya Vidmahe Shri Padmanaabhaaya Dheemahi |
Tanno Vishnuh Prachodayaat ||
content.meaning: We know Lord Purushottam (the Supreme Person), we meditate on Shri Padmanabha (the one from whose navel the lotus emerged). May Lord Vishnu inspire and guide us. This is the Purushottam Gayatri Mantra.
content.transliteration:
Om Puruṣottamāya Vidmahe Śrī Padmanābhāya Dhīmahi |
Tanno Viṣṇuḥ Pracodayāt ||

content.shloka:
Shantaakaaram Bhujagashayanam Padmanaabham Suresham |
Vishvaadhaarama Gaganasadrisham Meghavarnam Shubhaangam |
Lakshmikaantam Kamalanayanam Yogibhir Dhyaanagamyam |
Vande Vishnum Bhavabhayaharam Sarvalokaaikanaatham ||
content.meaning: I bow to Lord Vishnu — serene, reclining on Shesha, lotus-naveled, lord of gods, cosmic support, sky-vast, cloud-hued, beautiful, Lakshmi's beloved, lotus-eyed, attainable by yogis, destroyer of worldly fear, sole Lord of all worlds.
content.transliteration:
Śāntākāraṁ Bhujagaśayanaṁ Padmanābhaṁ Sureśam |
Viśvādhāraṁ Gaganasadṛśaṁ Meghavarṇaṁ Śubhāṅgam |
Lakṣmīkāntaṁ Kamalanayanam Yogibhir Dhyānagamyam |
Vande Viṣṇuṁ Bhavabhayaharaṁ Sarvalokaikanātham ||

content.shloka:
Mangalam Bhagavaan Vishnuh Mangalam Garudadhvajah |
Mangalam Pundareekakshah Mangalaaytanoh Harih ||
content.meaning: Auspicious is Lord Vishnu, auspicious is the one whose flag bears Garuda, auspicious is the lotus-eyed one, Hari is the abode of all auspiciousness. This mangala shloka concludes every Adhik Maas worship.
content.transliteration:
Maṅgalaṁ Bhagavān Viṣṇuḥ Maṅgalaṁ Garuḍadhvajaḥ |
Maṅgalaṁ Puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ Maṅgalāyatanaḥ Hariḥ ||

content.shloka:
Om Jai Jagadish Hare, Svami Jai Jagadish Hare |
Bhakta-jano ke sankat, daas-jano ke sankat,
Kshan men door kare | Om Jai Jagadish Hare ||
content.meaning: Victory to the Lord of the Universe. The troubles of devotees and servants are removed in an instant. Victory to the Lord of the Universe.
content.transliteration:
Om Jai Jagadīśa Hare, Svāmī Jai Jagadīśa Hare |
Bhakta-jano ke saṅkaṭ, dāsa-jano ke saṅkaṭ,
Kṣaṇ men dūr kare | Om Jai Jagadīśa Hare ||

content.shloka:
Jo dhyaave phal paave, dukh binase man kaa |
Sukh sampati ghar aave, kashta mite tan kaa |
Om Jai Jagadish Hare ||
content.meaning: Whoever meditates on the Lord receives the fruit, and sorrows of the mind are destroyed. Happiness and prosperity come to the home, and physical suffering is removed.
content.transliteration:
Jo dhyāve phal pāve, duḥkha binase man kā |
Sukha sampatī ghar āve, kaṣṭa miṭe tan kā |
Om Jai Jagadīśa Hare ||

content.shloka:
Maat pitaa tum mere, sharan gahun main kiski |
Tum bin aur na doojaa, aas karun main jiski |
Om Jai Jagadish Hare ||
content.meaning: You are my mother and father. Whose shelter should I seek? Besides You, there is no other in whom I can place my hopes.
content.transliteration:
Māt Pitā tum mere, śaraṇ gahūṁ maiṁ kiskī |
Tum bin aur na dūjā, ās karūṁ maiṁ jiskī |
Om Jai Jagadīśa Hare ||

content.shloka:
Tum pooran paramaaatmaa, tum antaryaamee |
Paar-Brahma Parameshwar, tum sab ke svaamee |
Om Jai Jagadish Hare ||
content.meaning: You are the complete Supreme Soul, You are the inner knower of all. You are the Supreme Brahman, the Lord of all beings.
content.transliteration:
Tum pūraṇ Paramātmā, tum Antaryāmī |
Pāra-Brahma Parameśvar, tum sab ke Svāmī |
Om Jai Jagadīśa Hare ||

content.shloka:
Vishay-vikar mitaao, paap haro devaa |
Shraddha bhakti badhaao, santan ki sevaa |
Om Jai Jagadish Hare ||

Om Jai Jagadish Hare, Svami Jai Jagadish Hare |
Bhakta-jano ke sankat, kshan men door kare |
Om Jai Jagadish Hare ||
content.meaning: Remove worldly attachments, destroy our sins, O Lord. Increase our faith and devotion, and our service to the saints. This aarti is sung during Adhik Maas puja every evening.
content.transliteration:
Viṣaya-vikār miṭāo, pāp haro Devā |
Śraddhā bhakti baḍhāo, santan kī sevā |
Om Jai Jagadīśa Hare ||
